summary: Client DoT probe blocked by AP client-isolation, causing internal service discovery failures for macOS clients
description: Issue summary: Several macOS laptops on the SF office Wi‑Fi could not resolve or reach internal services (internal-auth, build-cache, service-discovery) starting 2026-03-01 08:10 PST. Failure surface was DNS resolution and mDNS/TDNS-like discovery for zero-trust agent bootstrap. Impact: ~12 users reported inability to start development tools and SSO logins failing intermittently. No server-side incidents reported. Initial triage pointed to DNS failures from client hosts only over Wi‑Fi; wired clients unaffected.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect a macOS laptop (12.6+) to Redwood_SF_Guest SSID (configured with client isolation enabled)
2) Attempt to reach internal-auth.redwood.local via browser or curl (expected resolution to internal DNS)
3) Observe NXDOMAIN or long timeouts for SRV/TXT/DoT probes from client resolver
4) Connect same laptop to Redwood_SF_Employee (no isolation) or wired network and repeat: resolution succeeds
logs: Mar 01 08:14:22 client-resolver[6789]: dns-over-tls: handshake timeout connecting to 10.10.5.5:853
Mar 01 08:15:01 kernel: sandboxd[123]: network error: prevented outgoing TCP connection to 10.10.5.5:853 (AP client-isolation)
tcpdump (client, wlan0): TLS ClientHello to 10.10.5.5:853 then RST from AP, no SYN-ACK
investigation: 08:40 - Confirmed scope: only Wi‑Fi clients on SSID 'Redwood_SF_Guest' affected; wired and Employee SSID not impacted

08:52 - Reproduced with instrumentation: macOS resolver issues DoT probe to cluster DNS (10.10.5.5:853). AP responded with TCP reset when probe attempted to connect to 'server' IP in same VLAN but classified as 'peer-to-peer blocked' by guest policy

09:10 - AP config review: guest SSID had 'Client Isolation' and 'Block intra-VLAN TCP' enabled by default after recent firmware push (release 2026-02-27). Change log references 'tightened P2P policy' but did not call out DoT/TLS port exemptions

09:25 - Zero-trust agent (ZTA) behavior: agent attempts local DoT (systemd-resolved equivalent) to office DNS for split-horizon records; if DoT blocked, agent falls back to plaintext or mDNS heuristics but macOS resolver prevents fallback without user prompt, causing application failures
10:05 - Cross-check with AP vendor support: default client-isolation rule blocks TCP port 853 unless explicitly allowed via 'service exceptions' or ACL; firmware patch altered default rule behavior
10:40 - Temporary mitigation: updated AP SSID policy to allow TCP/853 and TCP/853 from clients to 10.10.5.0/24; immediately resolved DoT handshakes and restored service discovery
comments: 2026-03-01 09:00 - Aisha Patel: Customer reports coming in via #it-helpdesk. Early evidence looks like DNS failures over Wi‑Fi only. Assigning network team for AP policy check.

2026-03-01 09:30 - Miguel Reyes: Reproduced on my test MacBook. Captured tcpdump - client TLS ClientHello to 10.10.5.5:853 then RST from AP. Opening vendor TAC ticket for firmware change log. Moving to In Progress.

2026-03-01 10:45 - Network (Priya Singh): Applied ACL exception to Redwood_SF_Guest SSID for TCP/853 to office DNS cluster. Verified successful DoT handshake and ZTA bootstrap for 5 test clients. Monitoring for side effects.

2026-03-01 12:20 - Security (Liam Chen): Quick risk check: allowing TCP/853 internally should be fine; ensure rule scoped to 10.10.5.0/24 and logged. Recommend add to runbook if vendor defaults change again.

2026-03-04 15:10 - Miguel Reyes: Root cause confirmed with vendor: firmware 2.5.8 (2026-02-27) tightened P2P block semantics and no longer exempts TLS-based DoT flows. Patch 2.5.9 planned; we will keep SSID exception in place until firmware is validated. Closing incident.

2026-03-04 15:12 - Aisha Patel: Closing notes: outreach to office ops to communicate that Guest SSID retains TCP/853 exception. Add test to our Wi‑Fi configuration QA checklist to verify DoT behavior after future firmware upgrades.
resolution: Applied scoped ACL on Redwood_SF_Guest SSID to allow TCP port 853 to the office DNS subnet (10.10.5.0/24). Verified DoT handshakes and ZTA bootstrapping for affected macOS clients. Raised vendor TAC ticket; vendor acknowledged firmware change removed implicit DoT exemption and will release a follow-up. Added runbook step to test DoT and mDNS behavior post firmware upgrades. Incident resolved 2026-03-04.
